text:
deploy-bot: Starting config-only deploy: cfg-2026-03-midday. Changes: routing weight tweak (low->med), batch_max_tokens 4096->3072, per-request timeout 12s->10s. Canary: 5% traffic for 10m. /deploy cfg-2026-03-midday

james: copying notes — are we changing the routing policy name or just weights?

maya: weights only, route id stays 'fallback-fast'. small batch cap to reduce memory jitter. no model binary changes.

patrick: Can we pause canary until we confirm new timeout doesn't clip long-context ops? I saw a few >10s tails last week.

sarah: Observability pre-check: 99p latency for long prompts last week was 11.2s on svc-host-3. If we drop to 10s we might see truncated responses. Recommend canary only on low-context endpoints.

james: good catch. Suggest we make canary routing policy tag-based: header x-ctx: short -> canary, long -> stable. Quick config snippet: ```yaml
canary_policy:
  match:
    header: x-ctx
    equals: short
  traffic: 5%
  duration: 10m
```

maya: ack, I can patch the canary to include the header matcher. Will push config in 2 mins and trigger deploy-bot again.

deploy-bot: Received config push from maya. Running dry-run validations...

deploy-bot: Dry-run OK. Starting canary: routed 5% of requests matching header to new config. Canary window ends in 10m.

sarah: Live metric ping: canary latencies (p50/p95/p99): 48ms / 320ms / 1.1s on short-context. Errors: 0.1% 5xx (baseline 0.08%). Token per-request drop as expected.

james: I see a small error bump. Is that correlated to the routing change or batching cap? Can we pin routing to previous weight if it grows?

opsbot: Auto-rollback is armed. Thresholds: 5xx >0.5% OR p99 increase >200% for 5m -> rollback. Manual rollback command: `/rollback cfg-2026-03-midday`

maya: I audited the logs: spike is across two edge nodes only, likely transient GC. Not seeing request-level truncation. My plan: continue canary for another 5m, watch 5xx and p99. If stable, promote.

patrick: +1 for the extra 5. Also let's update the release notes with the routing header requirement and doc the fallback behavior.

deploy-bot: Canary still healthy at 5m mark: 5xx 0.12%, p99 +5%. No auto-rollback triggered.

sarah: Adding a quick eval: sample long-context requests against canary -> 0 truncations, but latency is up ~10% for long contexts when routed incorrectly. Confirm header-based matcher is critical.

james: Approved to promote to 50% on short-context only, pending 10m check. Keep stable for long-context.

maya: Promoting canary to 50% (short-context traffic). Pushing config change now: `update routing weights -> 50% canary short-context`

deploy-bot: Promotion applied. New traffic split active.

sarah: Monitoring: short-context p99 holds ~1.2s, 5xx 0.11%. No regressions observed.

james: ok, let's keep this config in canary for the remainder of the change window (end of day). If nothing else, we can roll to 100% tomorrow morning.

patrick: Roadmap note: add automated rule to auto-apply header tagging at the client SDK level to avoid human error.

maya: will follow up with a PR to the SDK this afternoon.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed to targeted canary scope. No rollback executed. Remember to add the cfg-2026-03-midday entry to release notes and tag the config in the db: `config.tag: midday-routing-shim`.

james: done — release notes updated and config tagged. Thanks all :rocket:
